note: Certified spans cut short by a sentence splitter that read an ABBREVIATION as a sentence end. This is a SEGMENTATION defect, not a classification one: every span here was already certified in the right section, on the right drop, with the right count. Only where the span stopped was wrong.
why: Q writes "Mr. President", "Army Lt. Gen. Paul Nakasone", "Al Franken - Democratic U.S. Senate", "Harris v. McRae", "GOOD vs. EVIL." A splitter that ends a sentence at "." cuts every one of them at the abbreviation. #4898 was certified as "Why is the FBI's top child porn lawyer involved in the H." and painted only that far. Recorded here rather than fixed in the deriving audits, for the same reason every other owner overlay is: a correction written into a re-derivable artifact is erased the next time its audit runs.
rule: The full span is taken FROM THE DROP, never retyped. Starting at the truncated span, extend one sentence-terminator at a time while the span still ENDS in an abbreviation; stop at the first real sentence end, or take the rest of the line when there is none. Iterative, because a span can be cut twice ("Army Lt." -> "Army Lt. Gen." -> "Army Lt. Gen. Paul Nakasone").
withdrawalRule: The SAME splitter certified the tail of each broken span as a span of its own, so repairing the head alone would leave one sentence certified twice - once whole, once as a fragment. That is the same-category overlap the owner ruled against on 2026-08-21. The fragment is absorbed into the full span, not deleted: the same words are certified once instead of twice.
abbreviations: single initials (A. Merkel, H. Biden, N. Korea)
falsePositivesExcluded: A span is only truncated if the DROP LINE CONTINUES past it. Complete Q lines that merely end in an abbreviation-shaped token - "No.", "Right on Q.", "Picture provides 40,000ft. v." - are left exactly as certified. 179 spans matched the shape; 107 were genuinely cut.
provenance: owner ruling on #4898 ("this should be a full question but is partially highlighted"), extended across every semantic category on the owner's direction of 2026-08-21.
supersedes: audit/questions-segmentation-fixes.json — its 10 repairs and 8 withdrawals are carried in here so this is the one record of the class.

repairs.truncated: "The immunity of a state from suit has long been held not to extend to actions against state officials for damages arising out of willful and negligent disregard of state laws.165 The reach of the rule is evident in Scheuer v.
repairs.full: "The immunity of a state from suit has long been held not to extend to actions against state officials for damages arising out of willful and negligent disregard of state laws.165 The reach of the rule is evident in Scheuer v. Rhodes,166 in which the Court held that plaintiffs were not barred by the Eleventh Amendment or other immunity doctrines from suing the governor and other officials of a state alleging that they deprived plaintiffs of federal rights under color of state law and seeking damages, when it was clear that plaintiffs were seeking to impose individual and personal liability on the officials.
repairs.dropLine: "The immunity of a state from suit has long been held not to extend to actions against state officials for damages arising out of willful and negligent disregard of state laws.165 The reach of the rule is evident in Scheuer v. Rhodes,166 in which the Court held that plaintiffs were not barred by the Eleventh Amendment or other immunity doctrines from suing the governor and other officials of a state alleging that they deprived plaintiffs of federal rights under color of state law and seeking damages, when it was clear that plaintiffs were seeking to impose individual and personal liability on the officials. There was no “executive immunity” from suit, the Court held; rather, the immunity of state officials is qualified and varies according to the scope of discretion and responsibilities of the particular office and the circumstances existing at the time the challenged action was taken."
